summary: ASTRA Flight Surgeon is a project designed to help protect astronauts' health during long space missions. It uses AI to monitor important health indicators, detect unusual changes, and provide alerts and medical insights to support astronauts and flight surgeons. I believe this project is important because space exploration comes with serious health challenges, especially when astronauts are far away from medical assistance. I wanted to contribute to a solution that could help identify potential health risks earlier and make astronauts feel safer during their missions.
details: ASTRA Flight Surgeon is a project designed to monitor the health of an astronaut during a long-duration space mission. It works by simulating continuous health data, including heart rate, CRP, fibrinogen, and hs-Troponin I, and comparing these values with predefined thresholds. When an unusual change is detected, the system generates an alert and uses AI to provide an explanation of the event, possible causes related to microgravity, recommended actions, and a monitoring plan. The information is displayed on a real-time dashboard, and the system can also generate a PDF medical incident report. The main benefit is that it helps identify potential health problems earlier, organize medical information, and support astronauts when communication with Earth is delayed. Our intended impact is to contribute to safer long-duration missions, especially future missions to the Moon and Mars. To develop the project, we used Python and FastAPI for simulated data generation, Java with Spring Boot for the backend, React for the frontend, PostgreSQL for data storage, OpenAI API for AI analysis, Recharts for visualizations, jsPDF for reports, and Docker Compose to run the different services together. What makes our project creative is the combination of health monitoring, automatic alerts, AI-powered explanations, and medical reporting in one platform. We also considered important factors such as the health risks of microgravity, the need for early detection, communication delays, ease of use, and astronaut safety. Since we do not have access to continuous real in-flight medical data, our current version uses simulated data, and all results are clearly labelled as simulated. The AI is designed to support decision-making, not replace the flight surgeon, and serious alerts are always escalated to medical professionals.
